[Presidential elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_election "United States presidential election") were held in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") on November 3, 2020.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-ElectionDay-1) The [Democratic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)") ticket of former [vice president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_President_of_the_United_States "Vice President of the United States")[Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden") and [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California") junior [senator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate")[Kamala Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamala_Harris "Kamala Harris") defeated the incumbent [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)")[president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States")[Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") and vice president [Mike Pence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pence "Mike Pence").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-12) The election saw the highest [voter turnout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voter_turnout_in_United_States_presidential_elections "Voter turnout in United States presidential elections") by percentage [since 1900](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1900_United_States_presidential_election "1900 United States presidential election"). Biden received more than 81 million votes,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-:7-13) the [most votes ever cast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_presidential_candidates_by_number_of_votes_received "List of United States presidential candidates by number of votes received") for a presidential candidate in U.S. history.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-:8-14)

In a competitive primary that featured the most candidates for any political party in the [modern era of American politics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sixth_Party_System "Sixth Party System"), Biden secured the [Democratic presidential nomination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Democratic_Party_presidential_primaries "2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries"). Biden's running mate, Harris, became the first African American, first Asian American, and third female[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-15) vice presidential nominee on a major party ticket. Trump easily secured re-nomination with only minor opposition in the [Republican primaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Republican_Party_presidential_primaries "2020 Republican Party presidential primaries"). [Jo Jorgensen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Jorgensen "Jo Jorgensen") secured the [Libertarian presidential nomination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Libertarian_Party_presidential_primaries "2020 Libertarian Party presidential primaries") with [Spike Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spike_Cohen "Spike Cohen") as her running mate, and [Howie Hawkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howie_Hawkins "Howie Hawkins") secured the [Green presidential nomination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Green_Party_presidential_primaries "2020 Green Party presidential primaries") with [Angela Nicole Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Nicole_Walker "Angela Nicole Walker") as his running mate.

The central issues of the election included the public health and [economic impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_impact_of_the_COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_United_States "Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States"), [civil unrest in reaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Floyd_protests "George Floyd protests") to the police [murder of George Floyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder_of_George_Floyd "Murder of George Floyd"), the [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States "Supreme Court of the United States") following the [death of Ruth Bader Ginsburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_and_state_funeral_of_Ruth_Bader_Ginsburg "Death and state funeral of Ruth Bader Ginsburg") and [confirmation of Amy Coney Barrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amy_Coney_Barrett_Supreme_Court_nomination "Amy Coney Barrett Supreme Court nomination"), and the future of the [Affordable Care Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affordable_Care_Act "Affordable Care Act").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-16) Due to the ongoing pandemic, a record number of ballots were [cast early](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_voting "Early voting") and [by mail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postal_voting "Postal voting").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-:9-17) Thirty-eight states had over half of all votes cast using these methods, and only three states had fewer than 25%.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-18) As a result of a large number of mail-in ballots, some [swing states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swing_state "Swing state") saw delays in vote counting and reporting; this led to major news outlets delaying their projection of Biden and Harris as the [president-elect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_transition_of_Joe_Biden "Presidential transition of Joe Biden") and [vice president-elect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_president-elect_of_the_United_States "Vice president-elect of the United States") until the morning of November 7, 2020.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-math-19)

Biden defeated Trump, winning 306 [Electoral College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Electoral_College "United States Electoral College") votes and 51.3% of the popular vote to Trump's 232 electoral votes and 46.8% of the popular vote. Trump was the first president to lose re-election since [George H. W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush") in [1992](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_United_States_presidential_election "1992 United States presidential election"). Key to Biden's pivotal victory were his wins in the Democratic-leaning [Rust Belt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_Belt "Rust Belt") states of [Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election_in_Michigan "2020 United States presidential election in Michigan"), [Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election_in_Pennsylvania "2020 United States presidential election in Pennsylvania"), and [Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election_in_Wisconsin "2020 United States presidential election in Wisconsin"), which Trump narrowly carried in 2016 and whose combined 46 electoral votes were enough to swing the election to either candidate. This election marked the first time since [1948](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_United_States_presidential_election "1948 United States presidential election") that the Democratic candidate won the popular vote in four consecutive elections.

Trump refused to accept the results; he and his allies made disproven claims of fraud, pressured election officials, filed several unsuccessful lawsuits,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-20)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-21)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-22) and directly [attempted to overturn the results](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attempts_to_overturn_the_2020_United_States_presidential_election "Attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election") at the county, state, and federal level. This culminated in an [attack on the United States Capitol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_6_United_States_Capitol_attack "January 6 United States Capitol attack") on January 6, 2021, for which [Trump was impeached a second time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_impeachment_of_Donald_Trump "Second impeachment of Donald Trump"). The day after the attack, Trump stated that a "new administration" would be succeeding his, without mentioning president-elect Biden by name, in a video posted on [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-23)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-24)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-25)

## Background

Further information: [United States presidential election §Procedure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_election#Procedure "United States presidential election")

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/56/Donald_Trump_official_portrait.jpg/250px-Donald_Trump_official_portrait.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Donald_Trump_official_portrait.jpg)

[Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump"), the incumbent president in 2020, whose first non-consecutive term expired at noon on January 20, 2021

The [Maine Legislature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine_Legislature "Maine Legislature") passed a bill in August 2019 adopting [ranked-choice voting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranked-choice_voting_in_the_United_States "Ranked-choice voting in the United States") (RCV) both for presidential primaries and for the general election.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-ovz9x-26)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-qhJpi-27) Governor [Janet Mills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Mills "Janet Mills") allowed the bill to become law without her signature, which delayed its taking effect until after the [2020 Democratic primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Maine_Democratic_primary "2020 Maine Democratic primary") in March and made Maine the first state to use RCV for a presidential general election. The [Maine Republican Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine_Republican_Party "Maine Republican Party") filed signatures for a [veto referendum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veto_referendum "Veto referendum") to preclude the use of RCV for the 2020 election, but [Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine_Secretary_of_State "Maine Secretary of State")[Matthew Dunlap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_Dunlap "Matthew Dunlap") found there were insufficient valid signatures to qualify for the ballot. A challenge in [Maine Superior Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine_Superior_Court "Maine Superior Court") was successful for the Maine Republican Party, but the [Maine Supreme Judicial Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine_Supreme_Judicial_Court "Maine Supreme Judicial Court")[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-28)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-29) stayed the ruling pending appeal on September 8, 2020.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-30) Nevertheless, ballots began being printed later that day without the veto referendum and including RCV for the presidential election,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-31)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-forbes-32) and the Court ruled in favor of the secretary of state on September 22, allowing RCV to be used.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-33) An emergency appeal to the [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States "Supreme Court of the United States") was denied on October 6.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-34) The law continues the use of the [congressional district method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_district_method "Congressional district method") for the allocation of Maine's electors ([Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebraska "Nebraska") is the only other state that apportions its electoral votes this way).[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-FcJYG-35) While multiple rounds of vote counting were not needed due to a single candidate receiving a majority of first-choice votes statewide and in each district, use of RCV complicates interpretation of the national [popular vote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct_election "Direct election") because voters are more likely to vote for third-party or independent candidates.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-36)

On December 14, 2020, pledged electors for each candidate, known collectively as the [United States Electoral College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Electoral_College "United States Electoral College"), gathered in their states' capitols to cast their official votes. Pursuant to the processes laid out by the [Electoral Count Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electoral_Count_Act "Electoral Count Act") of 1887, [certificates of ascertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Certificate_of_ascertainment "Certificate of ascertainment") listing the names of the electors and separate certificates recording their votes are distributed to various officials across the branches of government.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-37)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-38)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-39) The newly elected Congress, with the vice president in his role as Senate president presiding, met in a [joint session](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_session_of_the_United_States_Congress "Joint session of the United States Congress") to formally open the certificates and count the votes, which began on January 6, 2021, was interrupted by the [January 6 United States Capitol attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_6_United_States_Capitol_attack "January 6 United States Capitol attack"), and finished the following day.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-40)

### Democratic Party

Main articles: [2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Democratic_Party_presidential_primaries "2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries"), [2020 Democratic Party vice presidential candidate selection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Democratic_Party_vice_presidential_candidate_selection "2020 Democratic Party vice presidential candidate selection"), [2020 Democratic National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Democratic_National_Convention "2020 Democratic National Convention"), and [Joe Biden 2020 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden_2020_presidential_campaign "Joe Biden 2020 presidential campaign")

The Democratic Party chose its nominee in the [2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Democratic_Party_presidential_primaries "2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries"). [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden") became the [presumptive nominee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presumptive_nominee_(United_States) "Presumptive nominee (United States)") of the Democratic Party on April 8, 2020, after senator [Bernie Sanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernie_Sanders "Bernie Sanders") of [Vermont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vermont "Vermont") withdrew from the race.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-41) On June 5, 2020, Biden secured enough delegates to ensure his nomination at the national convention.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-42) Biden picked [Kamala Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamala_Harris "Kamala Harris") as his vice-presidential nominee, and the ticket was formally nominated at the convention on August 18.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_presidential_election#cite_note-43)
